full_judgment:
This Rule has arisen out of an order passed by the learned Munsif, 1st Court, Dhaka, allowing an application for adjournment of hearing for addition of some co-sharers by inheritance as opposite-parties in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 4. It appears that on the date of hearing of the application for pre-emption while P.W. I was being examined the pre-emptor-oppo-the parties filed an application stating that some co-sharers by inheritance had not been impleaded in the proceeding and that they should he made parties to arrive at a final decision of the case, and he prayed for one mouth's time for impleading the remaining co-sharers. The learned Munsif after hearing the patties adjourned the hearing of the case and allowed time for taking steps for the purpose. The provision under the sub-section 2 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as to impleading of all co-sharers of the holding as parties to the proceeding is obviously for the purpose of giving facility of pre-emption to the persons who have not exercised their right of pre-emption as provided under sub-section I of section 96 of the Act. It is however, mandatory on the part of the pre-emptor-opposite parties to implead all co-sharer tenants of the holding and the transferee, and if the pre-emptor is a contiguous owner of the land transferred all other owners contiguous to the land transfer-red and the transferee shall be made parties to the proceeding. This view has been finally set at rest by a decision of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh reported in 33 D.L.R, (A.D.) 113. 

 9. From the aforesaid observations of the Appellate Division it appears to me that the question of addition of a remaining co-sharer in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act cannot, be said to be closed, and addition of a remaining co-sharer can, be allowed after the application for pre-emption leas been filed and the period prescribed for filing such application has lapsed. In the aforesaid decision of the Appellate Division the pre-emptor failed to amend the application by impleading the remaining co-sharer in the proceeding and it continued without him. In my view, the period prescribed for filing the application for pre-emption relates to vis-a-vis the pre-emptor and the purchaser. This view finds support in the decision of a single Bench of this Court reported in 19 D.L.R. (H.C) 655. I am further of the opinion that for the purpose of impleading a remaining co-sharer in a proceeding under section 96 of the Ad the period of limitation as provided in sub-section (I) of section 96 of the State. Acquisition and Tenancy Act in filing an application for pre-emption by a pre-emptor against a purchaser for pre-empting the latter's kabala shall not apply.
